text:
ops-bot: Canary rollout started: release/new-routing @ 2026-03-15T12:30Z -> 40% traffic. Observability: canary metrics streaming to telemetry cluster A.
maya: seeing a bunch of 504s and backend error spikes in cloudfront logs, paging SRE.
aj: oncall here, getting alert storm for requests.service.504-rate high. Are we sure this is canary traffic?
maya: believing so, traffic tag header `x-canary-rollout: new-routing` present. But dashboard for canary doesn't show per-cluster breakdown — panels are blank.
kendall: I can confirm the dashboard missing tiles — the query fails with "no datasource" for the canary.kv namespace. Might be a dash variable that didn't materialize when the dashboard was cloned for the canary.
aj: oof. So we have noisy 504 alerts, but we can't tie to canary? That's dangerous for rollout decisions.
charlie: product impact report: two customers reported slow requests in EU region. No user-facing errors captured in Sentry yet, just increased latency/timeouts.
maya: can someone flip the kill-switch for the flag if this is definitely caused by the canary? Where's the safe rollback path?
aj: putting up the immediate mitigation checklist: 1) reduce canary to 0% (kill flag), 2) pause related autoscaling policies, 3) revert routing rule if needed. I'll try kill first.
aj: running kill command against FF service:  
```bash
curl -X POST https://flags.internal.redwood/v1/flags/new-routing/actions -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" -d '{"action":"disable"}'
```
ops-bot: Feature flag new-routing -> disable: accepted. Change propagated to control plane.
maya: Confirmed headers showing x-canary-rollout dropping to 0% in sample traces. But 504 alert persists in the next minute.
kendall: dashboards still not showing per-canary metrics. The SLO burn dashboard is showing high error budget spend but it's aggregated across all clusters — can't disambiguate. Need to know whether this is isolated to canary or hitting primary.
charlie: customers still seeing intermittent failures; we should open an incident page and notify CS to update status page.
aj: opening incident: https://incident.internal/redwood/INC-20260315-002 (created). Paging rotation: eng-oncall + eng-sre.
inc-bot: Incident INC-20260315-002 created by aj: "Canary rollout: elevated 504 rate, dashboards missing canary breakdown; kill-switch executed; customers impacted". Severity: SEV2.
maya: quick notes: logs show backend pool "model-vec" returned 502/503 sometimes; upstream service timeouts spike immediately when rollout reached 35-40% traffic. However after kill, errors declined but not fully resolved.
aj: I'm assigning kendall and maya to triage telemetry gap (dash + kibana datasource). Charlie, can you coordinate with CS on customer messaging?
charlie: pinging @cs-team. I'll prepare an interim status: investigating degraded API performance; we have reduced a recent routing change and are investigating root cause. ETA 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kendall: quick workaround for dashboards: switching template var to use global cluster tag works to show counts, but per-canary tag still not resolved because the data enrichment job for canary-tagging failed earlier today. I'm kickstarting that job now.
maya: any chance the enrichment job failure is why we couldn't see canary tiles? Makes sense.
aj: good find. If enrichment failure persisted, not only dashboards but alerting rules that rely on canary namespace would have misfired (explains noisy alerts).
kendall: enrichment job logs show 429 on the telemetry API when processing high cardinality tags — rate limit hit. I'm increasing retry/backoff and will re-run on a small window to backfill.
aj: for mitigation timeline: 1) flag disabled @12:35Z (done) 2) enrichment job re-run @12:50Z (in progress) 3) re-evaluate alerts after backfill @13:05Z. If errors continue, escalate to infra-owner.
maya: what's the plan for pages — do we keep SRE paged for now? Alerts are noisy and we can't make decisions without correct signal.
aj: I'm going to mute the noisy 504 alert rule for the next 30m while we validate the backfill; create a high-fidelity canary-only alert that will fire if new-routing-specific errors spike (once backfill completes).
kendall: muting rule done. Creating temporary canary-only rule (will rely on backfilled tags).
charlie: CS notified, initial status posted. Two customers acknowledged. We're tracking to provide a follow-up when we have root cause.
inc-bot: Update: engineers report kill-switch executed; telemetry enrichment re-run started; noisy alerts muted; CS informed.
aj: next steps: 1) complete enrichment backfill and confirm canary attribution 2) examine upstream service capacity (model-vec) for overload at ~40qps 3) root cause postmortem draft. Assigning owners: telemetry — kendall, infra capacity — maya, customer comms — charlie, postmortem — aj.
maya: preliminary hypothesis: the new-routing path increased concurrent connections to model-vec beyond a hotspot threshold causing head-of-line timeouts; combined with enrichment backfill failure, we lacked canary visibility.
kendall: agreed. I'll include the 429 throttling and telemetry backfill timeline in postmortem.
charlie: customer outreach: we offered workaround and escalated to priority support for affected accounts.
aj: closing timeline notes: last visible error drop observed @13:10Z, but SLO burn still shows a +0.8% delta — we'll keep monitoring. Last update to incident page in 15m.
inc-bot: Incident INC-20260315-002 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
maya: thanks team. We should add a checklist item to the release playbook: verify enrichment pipeline and dashboard template variables before traffic ramp.
kendall: noted — will draft release preflight check PR.
aj: nice work. We'll follow up with a postmortem once we have full backfill data. :thumbsup:
